title: Pangolin for Linux: Desktop Client with Tray Menu
summary: The Pangolin desktop client is now available on Linux, with deb, rpm, and Arch packages, a system tray menu, a settings window, and companion mode for Pangolin CLI.
body_markdown:
Pangolin now has a desktop client for Linux. Until now, connecting a Linux machine as a user device meant using Pangolin CLI. The new app gives you a tray icon for connecting and switching organizations, a settings window, in-app updates, and a background service that manages the tunnel. It runs on GNOME, KDE Plasma, and XFCE, under both X11 and Wayland.


[Download Pangolin for Linux](https://pangolin.net/downloads/linux) or grab a package from the[GitHub releases](https://github.com/fosrl/windows-linux/releases) .


## Release Highlights


### Packages for Debian, Fedora, openSUSE, and Arch


The client ships as` .deb` ,` .rpm` , and Arch` .pkg.tar.zst` packages for both amd64 and arm64. The quickest way to install it is the install script, which detects your distribution and architecture, downloads the right package, and installs it with your package manager:


```text
curl -fsSL https://static.pangolin.net/get-linux.sh | sh


```


If you'd rather install the package yourself, download it from the[downloads page](https://pangolin.net/downloads/linux) and install it from the folder you saved it to:


```text
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo   apt install ./pangolin-client-< arch  >-<version>.deb


# Fedora
sudo   dnf install ./pangolin-client-< arch  >-<version>.rpm


# openSUSE
sudo   zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm ./pangolin-client-< arch  >-<version>.rpm


# Arch Linux
sudo   pacman -U ./pangolin-client-< arch  >-<version>.pkg.tar.zst


```


The package installs the app, an app menu entry, and a` pangolin-client` systemd service. The service runs as root and handles the tunnel, routes, and DNS, while the app runs as your user and talks to it. The service is enabled and started during install, so you can open Pangolin from your app menu and log in right away.


Supported distributions are Ubuntu 22.04 or later, Debian 12 or later, and current releases of Fedora, openSUSE, and Arch. RHEL 9 and its rebuilds don't ship WebKitGTK 4.1, which the app needs, so the package won't install there.


### Works the Same as Windows


The Linux and Windows clients are built from the same code in[fosrl/windows-linux](https://github.com/fosrl/windows-linux) . The tray menu, login flow, and settings window match what you already see on Windows, so a team that uses both gets the same experience on each.


From the tray menu you can log in, connect and disconnect, switch accounts and organizations, pick an exit node, and open the status view to see connected sites. The **More** menu has **Check for Updates…** and **Install Pangolin CLI…** .


**Preferences…** opens the settings window. It has tabs for preferences, connection status, accounts, logs, and version info.


Admins can set defaults for every user on a machine in` /etc/pangolin-client/pangolin.json` , and users can override most keys in` ~/.config/pangolin-client/pangolin.json` . The keys are the same ones the Windows client uses, so existing config can be reused. See the[Linux client docs](https://docs.pangolin.net/manage/clients/platforms/linux#config-file) for the full list.


When a new version is out, **Pangolin Update Available…** appears in the tray menu. Installing it downloads the new package, checks it against Pangolin's signed update manifest, and installs it with` apt-get` ,` dnf` ,` zypper` ,` rpm` , or` pacman` , depending on how you installed it.


### GNOME, KDE Plasma, and XFCE


On KDE Plasma and XFCE the tray icon shows up with no setup. Cinnamon and Budgie work the same way.


GNOME has no system tray, so the package includes a GNOME Shell extension that adds a Pangolin button to the top bar. Click it to open the Pangolin menu, or right-click it to quit. GNOME doesn't turn on new extensions automatically, so log out and back in once after installing, then enable it in the **Extensions** app or run:


```text
gnome-extensions  enable   pangolin@pangolin.net


```


### CLI Companion Mode


If you also use[Pangolin CLI](https://docs.pangolin.net/manage/clients/platforms/cli) , it now runs in companion mode when the desktop app is installed. The CLI uses the app's login and tunnel, so you sign in once in the app and run CLI commands as that same account. There's no separate` pangolin login` .


You can install the CLI from the tray under **More** > **Install Pangolin CLI…** . It goes to` /usr/local/bin/pangolin` . Members of the` sudo` ,` wheel` , or` admin` group can install it directly, and other users are asked for an administrator's password.


With the app logged in and connected, commands like SSH to a[private SSH resource](https://docs.pangolin.net/manage/resources/private/ssh) just work:


```text
pangolin ssh username@ alias


```


The CLI follows the account, organization, and exit node selected in the app, so you change those in the app. While companion mode is on,` pangolin login` ,` pangolin logout` , and` pangolin select` are blocked. Run` pangolin companion status` to see the current state.


If you'd rather have the CLI keep its own login, switch companion mode off:


```text
pangolin companion  disable


```


Turn it back on later with` pangolin companion enable` . On machines without the desktop app, the CLI works as it always has.


## Get Started


Install with` curl -fsSL https://static.pangolin.net/get-linux.sh | sh` or[download Pangolin for Linux](https://pangolin.net/downloads/linux) , then log in with your Pangolin Cloud account or your self-hosted Pangolin instance. Install steps, config keys, and uninstall instructions are in the[Linux client docs](https://docs.pangolin.net/manage/clients/platforms/linux) . The source is on GitHub at[fosrl/windows-linux](https://github.com/fosrl/windows-linux) , and bug reports are welcome there.
